- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)
- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- courier:changeset-analyzer: Delegate when a git diff needs changeset@3 entries. Input is the diff, optionally a linked spec@1, smith's criteria_evidence and the existing unreleased changesets. Returns one entry per user-visible outcome, an update to an existing entry, or a recommendation that none is needed. (Tools: All tools)
- courier:commit-analyzer: Delegate when staged git changes need a conventional commit message. Input is the staged diff. Returns JSON with commit_message, type, scope (or null), a breaking flag, and a reasoning scratchpad. (Tools: All tools)
- courier:pr-narrator: Delegate when committed or staged changes need a pull request title and body. Input is a git diff, optionally a linked spec@1 or requirement@1. Returns JSON with title, body, labels, and a reasoning scratchpad. (Tools: All tools)
- courier:release-summarizer: Delegate when changeset@3 entries need aggregating into a release. Input is the changeset@3 list, the prior version, and a YYYY-MM-DD date. Returns a release-artifact@3 with the computed version, consumer-facing summaries, and aggregated breaking_changes. (Tools: All tools)
- courier:review-preprocessor: Delegate before a PR is opened to assemble the review package. Input is the changeset diff, optionally a linked spec@1 or requirement@1, test results, and open questions. Returns JSON with diff_summary, linked_spec, test_results, open_questions, and reasoning. (Tools: All tools)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- mason:auditor: Delegate to audit a plugin directory for ecosystem conformance: manifests, declared files, agent structure, routing, contracts, instruction economy, shared linkage. Input is the plugin path. Read-only; returns a structured conformance report with evidence per check. (Tools: All tools)
- mason:evaluation-adjudicator: Delegate after an isolated fixture run completes. Compares the run's evidence with the hidden fixture oracle and returns a `harness-evaluation@2`. (Tools: All tools)
- mason:evaluation-runner: Delegate to run one fixed behavioral fixture in an isolated workspace. Input is the public fixture input; the answer key is withheld. Returns an `evaluation-run@1` for the adjudicator. (Tools: All tools)
- mason:scaffolder: Delegate to create a plugin or add one agent to an existing plugin. Input is a plugin ID and purpose, or an agent task and tier. Returns a JSON report of created files. (Tools: All tools)
- mason:schema-designer: Delegate to design a new JSON Schema for an inter-agent artifact. Input is what the artifact represents, who produces it, and who consumes it. Returns the schema object and a recommended filename, after checking ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/schemas/ for conflicts. (Tools: All tools)
- muse:auditor: Delegate when a drafted component spec@1 needs adversarial quality review before planning. Input is the spec@1 JSON. Returns an audit object: an issues array, each issue with a rewritten fix, and an overall pass/fail. Reviews the spec on its own terms, not against source artifacts. (Tools: All tools)
- muse:drafter: Delegate when a requirement@1 or free-text design intent needs a component spec@1 drafted; optional design references (mockup, component family, tokens). Returns the spec@1 object only. Also runs in correction mode: given spec_file_path, a criterion_id, and a contradiction report, returns the corrected spec@1 with revision_note. (Tools: All tools)
- muse:exit-gate: Delegate when an audited component spec@1 needs the binding pass/fail judgment before planning. Input is the spec@1 JSON. Returns a verdict@3 with artifact_type spec@1; a fail blocks progression to navigator until the spec is corrected and resubmitted. (Tools: All tools)
- muse:explorer: Delegate when a sketch needs one structurally different option built and rendered. Input is the anchor brief, committed direction, assigned structural idea, sibling options, option id and scratch directory. Returns an option-set@1 with only its option. Non-binding: no tests or spec; never ranks its option. (Tools: All tools)
- navigator:challenger: Delegate to this subagent when a plan@1 needs adversarial review before implementation. Input is a plan@1 and its source spec@1. Check missing work, dependency order, prescription, batching, error handling, criterion coverage, and interface siblings against live evidence. Return per-issue repairs and a binding pass or fail verdict. (Tools: All tools)
- navigator:estimator: Delegate when a plan@1 needs a rough effort estimate before execution. Returns JSON with per-task minutes, parallelizable flags, blocking task IDs, total_minutes, and an assumptions array. Assumes an implementer with full codebase context but no domain knowledge. (Tools: All tools)
- navigator:planner: Delegate when a completed spec@1 (or its spec_file_path) needs a dependency-ordered implementation plan. Returns a plan@1 of batched tasks, each with outcome, files, signatures, proving tests, and covers_criteria; code only where logic is non-obvious. Also runs in amend mode: given a plan@1, a corrected spec@1, and changed criterion_ids, it patches only affected tasks. Route output to challenger. (Tools: All tools)
- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- ranger:adversary: Delegate once per candidate@1 from scanner (after boundary-tracer for T7/T10) to try to refute its reachability against current code. Returns one candidate-assessment@1: confirmed with a concrete failing scenario, plausible when external state decides, or dismissed with the blocking guard. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:boundary-tracer: Delegate for scanner candidates in taxonomies T7 or T10 (dropped intent, downgraded errors) in Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or Go. Traces each field of the flagged type from construction to an execution boundary. Returns a field-survival-map@1 for the adversary. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:exit-gate: Delegate after remediation of a finding-report@2 to independently verify confirmed findings and their defect families against current code, including sibling sites and execution-boundary evidence. Plausible findings pass through to human review. Returns verdict@3. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:recon: Delegate first, before scanning. Detects affected languages, traces reachable files from live entry points, and inventories project capabilities and current workspace state. Makes no defect judgments. Returns workspace-manifest@1 listing live files. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:scanner: Delegate after recon with its workspace-manifest@1. Loads the hazard pack for each scoped language (Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go), searches only live files, and emits every match as a candidate@1 without judging it. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:arch-auditor: Delegate to check a draft spec@1 against whole-system architecture (module boundaries, canonical abstractions, cross-codebase invariants) before scribe/gate-spec; input is the spec plus workspace_root; returns arch-audit@1. Also builds or refreshes the persisted arch-model@2 when it is absent or a refresh is requested. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:architect: Delegate when `finding-report@2`, `implementation-review@2`, or `implementation-result@1` identifies a structural defect class. Inspect the live semantic model and persisted architecture, then produce a `spec@1` that makes recurrence impossible or machine-detectable. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:auditor: Delegate for adversarial quality review of a spec@1 on its own terms before planning: untestable, ambiguous, incomplete, overlapping, padded, or cross-spec round-trip gaps. Input is the spec@1; returns an issues array with rewritten fixes and a pass/fail verdict. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:drafter: Delegate to draft a formal spec@1 from a completed requirement@1 and optional research-report@1; returns the spec object only. Also runs in correction mode, given spec_file_path, a criterion_id, and implementer's contradiction report, returning the corrected spec@1 with revision_note. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:drift-checker: On-demand diagnostic, not a gate: given spec_file_path and a workspace root, checks whether current code and tests still satisfy each acceptance criterion, weeks or months after implementation. Optionally takes a prior changeset@2's criteria_evidence. Returns a drift report with covered, uncovered, and drifted arrays. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:exit-gate: Issue the binding `verdict@3` for a `spec@1` before planning. Pass only when every criterion is testable, error behavior is explicit, no TBD remains, scope fits one planning cycle, and all checks are complete. (Tools: All tools)
- scribe:verifier: Delegate to check that a draft spec@1 is grounded in its sources before auditing or gating. Input is the spec plus the originating requirement@1 and optional research-report@1; returns an evidence report classifying criteria as supported, unsupported, or overfitted, with no verdict. For post-implementation drift use drift-checker. (Tools: All tools)
- sentinel:exit-gate: Delegate with a completed verifier report to get the binding `verdict@3` for an artifact. Default disposition is fail; separates blockers, coverage gaps, and pending checks, and passes only within the verified scope. Returns `verdict@3` with actionable blockers on fail. (Tools: All tools)
- sentinel:recon: Delegate first in the sentinel gate, before verification, with an artifact path or description. Identifies the artifact type, locates it, enumerates the criteria to verify and the source files to cross-check; no judgment. Returns a JSON manifest for verifier. (Tools: All tools)
- sentinel:verifier: Delegate after recon, with its manifest (artifact path, criteria, source files). Collects evidence per criterion and classifies each as verified, failed, unverifiable, or pending; evidence only, no verdict. Returns a JSON evidence report for exit-gate. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:exit-gate: Delegate once every planned batch has a terminal result and an approved `implementation-review@2`. Independently checks current code, spec criteria, mutation evidence, sibling completeness, and pending work. Returns a scoped `verdict@3`. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:implementer: Delegate to implement and test one plan task or one fix-pass batch. Input: the task or brief, persisted spec paths, recon manifest, and any precision tests. Returns `implementation-result@1` with criteria_evidence; commits only when `commit_authorized: true`. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:mutator: Delegate after implementation to test whether the tests detect faults in changed behavior, using project-native mutation tooling or a controlled deliberate fault. Returns `mutation-report@2` with survivors, precision tests, and coverage gaps. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:recon: Delegate before any implementation edits. Inspects workspace state, languages, entry points, verification capabilities, baseline tests, and persisted artifact freshness. Returns `workspace-manifest@1`; stops on a failing baseline. (Tools: All tools)
- smith:reviewer: Delegate after an implementation batch and its mutation check. Reviews scope, verification fit, syntactic and semantic sibling defects, and architecture fit. Returns `implementation-review@2`; structural families route to `scribe:architect`. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- vanguard:reader: Delegate after recon produces a source map. Input is that map plus the original research question. Reads every mapped source and returns a JSON object of cited findings, each with a confidence level, plus sources_read and a reasoning scratchpad. Extracts only; route output to synthesizer. (Tools: All tools)
- vanguard:recon: Delegate at the start of any research task, before reading begins. Input is a requirement@1 or free-text research question. Maps which specs, docs, manifests, codebase patterns, or external sources likely answer it, and returns a JSON research agenda (source map) for reader. (Tools: All tools)
- vanguard:risk-assessor: Delegate when a proposed approach or research-report@1 needs risk review before a spec is written. Input is the approach or report, optionally with target-environment context. Returns a JSON object with a prioritized risks array (severity, likelihood, trigger, mitigation) and an overall_risk. (Tools: All tools)
- vanguard:synthesizer: Delegate after reader produces findings. Input is reader's findings array and reasoning plus the original research question. Synthesizes them into a research-report@1 with a falsifiable recommendation, confidence, contradictions, and open questions. Route output to scribe. (Tools: All tools)
- weaver:auditor: Delegate to cross-reference open requirement@1 objects against existing specs, persisted plans, and implementation files before planning. Input is a list of requirements, or one (or a few) for a narrower connect mode. Returns a read-only audit report with per-requirement status, evidence, and summary. (Tools: All tools)
- weaver:clarifier: Delegate when a requirement@1 draft from intake needs review for missing or underspecified dimensions before a spec can be written. Input is a requirement@1. Returns a JSON object with either one clarifying question or the completed requirement. Route completed requirements to drafter. (Tools: All tools)
- weaver:intake: Delegate when you have a raw need in free text (problem description, user story, feature request) and need a structured requirement@1 draft. Input is unstructured text. Returns a requirement@1 JSON object. Route it to clarifier before writing a spec. (Tools: All tools)
- weaver:prioritizer: Delegate when a set of requirement@1 drafts needs ranking before planning starts. Input is a list of requirement@1 objects. Returns an ordered list with a rationale per requirement and any dependency relationships found. (Tools: All tools)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

1

Callisto Architecture

2 3

Crate map, data flow, and the invariants every change must preserve.

4 5 --- 6 7 ## Invariants 8 9 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 10 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 11 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST. String-only `package.json` changes replace scanned literal spans in the original text; other changes keep key order and fingerprinted indentation and line endings. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 12 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent directory, and its parent when the call created it; a failed sync is returned unless the filesystem cannot sync a directory) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 13 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 14 6. **Versioning.** The four published crates version in lockstep (one fixed group). Only `callisto-cli`, its command-line interface and its JSON reports are a compatibility surface; `callisto-model`, `callisto-manifests` and `callisto-graph` are internal and may change in any release. 15 7. **User-facing errors are diagnosable.** Every error surfaced to a user derives `miette::Diagnostic` with a stable code and, where the fix isn't obvious from the message, `help` text. A wrapper around another crate's error (for example `GraphError::Config`) is `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and declares no code of its own, so the inner code reaches the user. Full list: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). 16 17 Design decisions, with the options they rejected and why: [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md). 18 19 ## Crate map 20 21 ``` 22 Layer 1 (leaf) callisto-model 23 Layer 2 (I/O) callisto-manifests 24 Layer 3 (engine) callisto-graph 25 Layer 4 (surface) callisto-cli 26 Dev-only callisto-fixtures 27 ``` 28 29 | Crate | License | Depends on | Purpose | 30 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | 31 | [`callisto-model`](crates/callisto-model) | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`) | Domain primitives (`PackageId`, `Version`, `Severity`, `Changeset`, `PreState`), `atomic_write`, `ApplyPermit`, the `CommandRunner`/`DependencyResolver` trait seams; `format`: `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` parser/writer; `vcs`: `GitAccess`, every Git operation as a subprocess through `CommandRunner` | 32 | [`callisto-manifests`](crates/callisto-manifests) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model | `Manifest` trait; format-preserving Cargo/npm/PyPI manifest editors | 33 | [`callisto-graph`](crates/callisto-graph) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests | Dependency graph, cascade engine, version planning, release execution; `conventional`: Conventional Commit parsing and bump inference; `changelog`: Markdown changelog rendering, with `changelog::markdown` the only place Markdown is scanned; `release_preview`: the serializable view of a plan for the release PR | 34 | [`callisto-cli`](crates/callisto-cli) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph | `clap` CLI surface, `miette` diagnostic rendering | 35 | [`callisto-fixtures`](crates/callisto-fixtures) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) | Multi-ecosystem test corpus and in-memory test doubles | 36 37 Dependencies only point down the layers (`cli` → `graph` → `manifests` → `model`). Nothing in Layer 1–3 depends on `callisto-cli`. 38 39 ## Data flow 40 41 ``` 42 Workspace::load 43 config::load -> config::resolve callisto.toml -> ResolvedConfig 44 ManifestWalkResolver::build discover (ProjectLocator), read manifests (Manifest), 45 assign ids, attach platform packages, apply per-package config 46 GroupTable::resolve bind [[fixed-group]] / [[linked-group]] members 47 plan_version -> VersionPlan (in memory) 48 aggregate changesets + opt-in commit inference -> severity per package 49 run_cascade dependents (runtime, build, optional, peer; never dev), groups, pre mode 50 -> target version per package, with its reasons 51 version --emit-decision derives and validates the decision in memory, before apply 52 version --emit-preview builds the ReleasePreview (packages, merged changes, findings) from the 53 plan, before apply consumes the changesets it describes 54 apply_version_plan (needs ApplyPermit) CST edits -> atomic_write, changelogs 55 consume changesets -> native lock refresh -> git staging 56 version --emit-decision / --emit-preview writes the decision and the preview files after successful apply 57 compose-pr-body --preview [--publish-plan] renders the release PR body from the preview; --publish-plan adds the 58 outcome of plan_workspace_release_offline on the versioned tree for 59 exactly the packages the preview bumps (never observes a registry) 60 release decision -> intent -> envelope -> execute_release -> receipt 61 per operation observe provider -> adopt, or perform and confirm 62 ``` 63 64 Package ordering, cycle reports and release-operation readiness all run on `michi-graph` (validation reports every problem at once; edge kinds are chosen per validation). Git access goes through `GitAccess` (`callisto_model::vcs`). Reads that cover every package are batched or run side by side, so a command's cost does not grow by a process or a round trip per package ([release](docs/architecture/release.md) lists them; `just bench` measures them). 65 66 Depth: 67 68 - [`docs/architecture/identity.md`](docs/architecture/identity.md): package ids, bare-name matching, config rule specificity, workspace loading, platform packages. 69 - [`docs/architecture/versioning.md`](docs/architecture/versioning.md): plan and apply, file-level idempotence and interrupted-command limits, the release preview and the Markdown module. 70 - [`docs/architecture/release.md`](docs/architecture/release.md): release terms, the two routes, run envelope, observation and proof tokens, the transition table, verification tiers. 71 - [`docs/architecture/wire-compat.md`](docs/architecture/wire-compat.md): the version each release document writes and reads, what a reader does with another, and the known gaps. 72 73 ## Extension seams 74 75 Four traits decouple the engine from platform I/O (`callisto-model::exec`, `callisto-model::discovery`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph::locate`): 76 77 - `ProjectLocator` — enumerates workspace project roots. 78 - `CommandRunner` — runs a subprocess. `run_with_timeout`'s default implementation ignores the timeout; the CLI's runner enforces it, so a hung publish command cannot block forever. 79 - `Manifest` — per-ecosystem read/write. Mutations only touch the in-memory CST; nothing reaches disk until `persist(&ApplyPermit)`, so one open manifest can take several mutations before one write. 80 - `DependencyResolver` — supplies graph nodes and edges; `ManifestWalkResolver` is the only current implementation. 81 82 ## Current boundaries and planned changes 83 84 `PackageId` is a flexible selector/display form; `PackageKey` is a directory locator; `ReleasePackageId` is a canonical ecosystem-qualified distribution identity. A directory can own several canonical manifests, but the current package model requires one version grammar. Registry version observations alone do not establish identical package bytes. CI can seal a Python file set in the artifact manifest and verify each file on execution. 85 86 Remaining v1 work is in [`docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md`](docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md). The canonical-identity and polyglot model is in [`docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md`](docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md); only the parts it marks as design are not implemented, and none is an extension seam. The existing dependency graph and release-operation DAG remain the basis of the plan. 87 88 ## Not covered here 89 90 - Release lifecycle, CI plan/build/execute, recovery: [`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md). 91 - Registry authentication: [`docs/publishing.md`](docs/publishing.md). 92 - `callisto.toml` keys: [`docs/config.md`](docs/config.md). 93 - Diagnostic codes: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). 94 - Behavior, including `callisto matrix`: [`docs/specs/`](docs/specs/INDEX.md). 95

Design decisions, with the options they rejected and why: [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md). ## Crate map ``` Layer 1 (leaf) callisto-model Layer 2 (I/O) callisto-manifests Layer 3 (engine) callisto-graph Layer 4 (surface) callisto-cli Dev-only callisto-fixtures ``` | Crate | License | Depends on | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`callisto-model`](crates/callisto-model) | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`) | Domain primitives (`PackageId`, `Version`, `Severity`, `Changeset`, `PreState`), `atomic_write`, `ApplyPermit`, the `CommandRunner`/`DependencyResolver` trait seams; `format`: `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` parser/writer; `vcs`: `GitAccess`, every Git operation as a subprocess through `CommandRunner` | | [`callisto-manifests`](crates/callisto-manifests) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model | `Manifest` trait; format-preserving Cargo/npm/PyPI manifest editors | | [`callisto-graph`](crates/callisto-graph) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests | Dependency graph, cascade engine, version planning, release execution; `conventional`: Conventional Commit parsing and bump inference; `changelog`: Markdown changelog rendering, with `changelog::markdown` the only place Markdown is scanned; `release_preview`: the serializable view of a plan for the release PR | | [`callisto-cli`](crates/callisto-cli) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph | `clap` CLI surface, `miette` diagnostic rendering | | [`callisto-fixtures`](crates/callisto-fixtures) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) | Multi-ecosystem test corpus and in-memory test doubles | Dependencies only point down the layers (`cli` → `graph` → `manifests` → `model`). Nothing in Layer 1–3 depends on `callisto-cli`. ## Data flow ``` Workspace::load config::load -> config::resolve callisto.toml -> ResolvedConfig ManifestWalkResolver::build discover (ProjectLocator), read manifests (Manifest), assign ids, attach platform packages, apply per-package config GroupTable::resolve bind [[fixed-group]] / [[linked-group]] members plan_version -> VersionPlan (in memory) aggregate changesets + opt-in commit inference -> severity per package run_cascade dependents (runtime, build, optional, peer; never dev), groups, pre mode -> target version per package, with its reasons version --emit-decision derives and validates the decision in memory, before apply version --emit-preview builds the ReleasePreview (packages, merged changes, findings) from the plan, before apply consumes the changesets it describes apply_version_plan (needs ApplyPermit) CST edits -> atomic_write, changelogs consume changesets -> native lock refresh -> git staging version --emit-decision / --emit-preview writes the decision and the preview files after successful apply compose-pr-body --preview [--publish-plan] renders the release PR body from the preview; --publish-plan adds the outcome of plan_workspace_release_offline on the versioned tree for exactly the packages the preview bumps (never observes a registry) release decision -> intent -> envelope -> execute_release -> receipt per operation observe provider -> adopt, or perform and confirm ``` Package ordering, cycle reports and release-operation readiness all run on `michi-graph` (validation reports every problem at once; edge kinds are chosen per validation). Git access goes through `GitAccess` (`callisto_model::vcs`). Reads that cover every package are batched or run side by side, so a command's cost does not grow by a process or a round trip per package ([release](docs/architecture/release.md) lists them; `just bench` measures them). Depth: - [`docs/architecture/identity.md`](docs/architecture/identity.md): package ids, bare-name matching, config rule specificity, workspace loading, platform packages. - [`docs/architecture/versioning.md`](docs/architecture/versioning.md): plan and apply, file-level idempotence and interrupted-command limits, the release preview and the Markdown module. - [`docs/architecture/release.md`](docs/architecture/release.md): release terms, the two routes, run envelope, observation and proof tokens, the transition table, verification tiers. - [`docs/architecture/wire-compat.md`](docs/architecture/wire-compat.md): the version each release document writes and reads, what a reader does with another, and the known gaps. ## Extension seams Four traits decouple the engine from platform I/O (`callisto-model::exec`, `callisto-model::discovery`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph::locate`): - `ProjectLocator` — enumerates workspace project roots. - `CommandRunner` — runs a subprocess. `run_with_timeout`'s default implementation ignores the timeout; the CLI's runner enforces it, so a hung publish command cannot block forever. - `Manifest` — per-ecosystem read/write. Mutations only touch the in-memory CST; nothing reaches disk until `persist(&ApplyPermit)`, so one open manifest can take several mutations before one write. - `DependencyResolver` — supplies graph nodes and edges; `ManifestWalkResolver` is the only current implementation. ## Current boundaries and planned changes `PackageId` is a flexible selector/display form; `PackageKey` is a directory locator; `ReleasePackageId` is a canonical ecosystem-qualified distribution identity. A directory can own several canonical manifests, but the current package model requires one version grammar. Registry version observations alone do not establish identical package bytes. CI can seal a Python file set in the artifact manifest and verify each file on execution. Remaining v1 work is in [`docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md`](docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md). The canonical-identity and polyglot model is in [`docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md`](docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md); only the parts it marks as design are not implemented, and none is an extension seam. The existing dependency graph and release-operation DAG remain the basis of the plan. ## Not covered here - Release lifecycle, CI plan/build/execute, recovery: [`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md). - Registry authentication: [`docs/publishing.md`](docs/publishing.md). - `callisto.toml` keys: [`docs/config.md`](docs/config.md). - Diagnostic codes: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). - Behavior, including `callisto matrix`: [`docs/specs/`](docs/specs/INDEX.md).

1	# Releasing
2	
3	How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.
4	
5	For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Local release: `callisto release`
10	
11	`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.
12	
13	- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
14	- `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, all distributions of each (naming `npm/dual` also releases `cargo/dual`), plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
15	- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
16	- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
17	- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
18	- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.
19	
20	`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.
21	
22	A local release refuses with E320, before any effect, when the registry already holds a version it would release but the package's files changed since the commit that set that version, or no commit in this history sets it. Check out the version commit the error names and run `callisto release` again: it adopts the published version and tags that commit. When no commit is named, check out the commit that was published, or tag it by hand.
23	
24	### Current retry limit
25	
26	If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.
27	
28	- `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
29	- Generated simple workflows share this limit.
30	- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Generated workflows
35	
36	`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.
37	
38	Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.
39	
40	- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
41	- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
42	- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.
43	
44	Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).
45	
46	Generated build support has these boundaries:
47	
48	- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
49	- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
50	- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
51	- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.
52	
53	The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.
54	
55	Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.
56	
57	Build-matrix limits:
58	
59	- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
60	- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
61	- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
62	- The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
63	- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Release PR and approval
68	
69	The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.
70	
71	The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).
72	
73	Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.
74	
75	After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.
76	
77	## PR pre-flight verification
78	
79	[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:
80	
81	- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
82	- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
83	- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Release identity and recovery
88	
89	Every release run records two different revisions:
90	
91	- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
92	- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.
93	
94	A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and the merged release PR's full source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code or invent a newer version. Callisto's own workflow asks [`callisto release pending`](#finding-releases-that-did-not-finish) for the oldest unfinished release on each main push. It verifies that SHA against the merged managed PR and the current main history before planning. After a release executes, the workflow dispatches the next unfinished one, or refreshes the release PR for newer changesets when none remains.
95	
96	To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs" or dispatch the workflow on main with `release_source_sha=<merged PR merge SHA>`. Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds. The merge SHA is available in the PR's merge commit and does not depend on a proposed version tag. Release runs execute one at a time: a push during a release waits, then finds nothing pending. A dispatch with an explicit SHA queued behind a push can be replaced by it, so dispatch it again if it did not start.
97	
98	A failed release is selected again on every main push until it finishes, which also holds back the release PR refresh. To get past one you finished by hand, push its missing tags, or run `callisto release pending --from <newer release sha>`. Otherwise recover it with a dispatch of its SHA (see [recovering an older release](#recovering-an-older-release)). Finish an older unpublished release before merging a newer release PR: the newer one publishes without any warning that the older version was never tagged.
99	
100	Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.
101	
102	## Finding releases that did not finish
103	
104	`callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. It reads each release commit's committed decision and checks that every package has its tag and every GitHub release is published, so it needs no checkout of the old commit and publishes nothing. A release publishes to the registries before it tags, so a missing tag means the release stopped early.
105	
106	```sh
107	callisto release pending                    # text
108	callisto --format json release pending      # for a workflow
109	callisto release pending --from <sha>       # skip an older release that cannot finish
110	```
111	
112	Recover each one with the dispatch below, oldest first.
113	
114	## A stale release PR
115	
116	Callisto's workflow rebuilds the release PR on every push to `main`. While that rebuild is pending the PR is stale: if changesets changed on `main` since it was built, merging it releases the wrong set. So a second workflow, `Hold release PR`, turns the open release PR into a draft the moment `main` moves, and the release workflow marks it ready only after a rebuild from the new tip. If the rebuild fails, the PR stays a draft and cannot be merged. Re-run that `Release` workflow run, and the PR becomes ready when it succeeds. A transient GitHub error during the rebuild is attempted up to four times in all before it fails.
117	
118	If a stale release PR was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the merge consumed no changesets, and every later push to `main` retries it. Nothing was published. Revert the merge's release payload (the version bumps, changelog entries and `.callisto/release-decision.json`, not the changeset files) in a pull request to `main`. The next push rebuilds the release PR from the changesets that are really pending.
119	
120	## Recovering an older release
121	
122	Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:
123	
124	**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:
125	
126	```sh
127	SHA=<release-source sha>
128	git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
129	git push origin "<tag>"
130	gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
131	```
132	
133	**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:
134	
135	```sh
136	gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
137	gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
138	```
139	
140	## Publication checks
141	
142	Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.
143	
144	Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).
145	
146	GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Platform-package publish order
151	
152	`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.
153	
154	A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.
155	
156	- **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
157	- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.
158	
159	For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.

# Releasing

How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.

For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).

---

## Local release: `callisto release`

`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.

- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
- `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, all distributions of each (naming `npm/dual` also releases `cargo/dual`), plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.

`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.

A local release refuses with E320, before any effect, when the registry already holds a version it would release but the package's files changed since the commit that set that version, or no commit in this history sets it. Check out the version commit the error names and run `callisto release` again: it adopts the published version and tags that commit. When no commit is named, check out the commit that was published, or tag it by hand.

### Current retry limit

If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.

- `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
- Generated simple workflows share this limit.
- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.

---

## Generated workflows

`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.

Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.

- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.

Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

Generated build support has these boundaries:

- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.

The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.

Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.

Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

## PR pre-flight verification

[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:

- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.

---

## Release identity and recovery

Every release run records two different revisions:

- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.

A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and the merged release PR's full source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code or invent a newer version. Callisto's own workflow asks [`callisto release pending`](#finding-releases-that-did-not-finish) for the oldest unfinished release on each main push. It verifies that SHA against the merged managed PR and the current main history before planning. After a release executes, the workflow dispatches the next unfinished one, or refreshes the release PR for newer changesets when none remains.

To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs" or dispatch the workflow on main with `release_source_sha=<merged PR merge SHA>`. Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds. The merge SHA is available in the PR's merge commit and does not depend on a proposed version tag. Release runs execute one at a time: a push during a release waits, then finds nothing pending. A dispatch with an explicit SHA queued behind a push can be replaced by it, so dispatch it again if it did not start.

A failed release is selected again on every main push until it finishes, which also holds back the release PR refresh. To get past one you finished by hand, push its missing tags, or run `callisto release pending --from <newer release sha>`. Otherwise recover it with a dispatch of its SHA (see [recovering an older release](#recovering-an-older-release)). Finish an older unpublished release before merging a newer release PR: the newer one publishes without any warning that the older version was never tagged.

Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.

## Finding releases that did not finish

`callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. It reads each release commit's committed decision and checks that every package has its tag and every GitHub release is published, so it needs no checkout of the old commit and publishes nothing. A release publishes to the registries before it tags, so a missing tag means the release stopped early.

```sh
callisto release pending                    # text
callisto --format json release pending      # for a workflow
callisto release pending --from <sha>       # skip an older release that cannot finish
```

Recover each one with the dispatch below, oldest first.

## A stale release PR

Callisto's workflow rebuilds the release PR on every push to `main`. While that rebuild is pending the PR is stale: if changesets changed on `main` since it was built, merging it releases the wrong set. So a second workflow, `Hold release PR`, turns the open release PR into a draft the moment `main` moves, and the release workflow marks it ready only after a rebuild from the new tip. If the rebuild fails, the PR stays a draft and cannot be merged. Re-run that `Release` workflow run, and the PR becomes ready when it succeeds. A transient GitHub error during the rebuild is attempted up to four times in all before it fails.

If a stale release PR was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the merge consumed no changesets, and every later push to `main` retries it. Nothing was published. Revert the merge's release payload (the version bumps, changelog entries and `.callisto/release-decision.json`, not the changeset files) in a pull request to `main`. The next push rebuilds the release PR from the changesets that are really pending.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh
gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

## Publication checks

Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.

Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.

---

## Platform-package publish order

`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.

A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.

- **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.

For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.

1	# Publishing: registry authentication
2	
3	Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).
4	
5	Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## First publish
10	
11	A package that has never been published is released from its manifest version with no changeset. Callisto plans it like any other release, and the first publish is the one most likely to fail for reasons outside Callisto:
12	
13	- **Check the name first.** A name another project already owns is rejected by the registry. If it already holds the version you are releasing under another repository, `callisto release` stops with E322 and names that repository. Search the registry before the first release.
14	- **Fill in the metadata the registry requires.** crates.io needs `description` and `license` (or `license-file`) in `Cargo.toml`. A first release of a crate without them stops with E323 before anything is published.
15	- **Use a token that can create the package.** A token scoped to existing packages cannot publish a new one. Trusted publishing (OIDC) is configured per package on the registry and generally needs the package, or a pending publisher, to exist first, so plan on one token-based first publish. Follow each registry's current documentation.
16	- **Package managers.** An npm package is published with the manager its workspace uses (`npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` 4 or `bun`), passing `--tag`, `--access` and, where the manager takes one, `--registry`. Yarn takes no `--registry`; it reads `publishConfig.registry` from the package itself.
17	- **Scoped npm packages** publish with `--access public` by default. A private scoped package sets `publishConfig.access` to `"restricted"` in its `package.json`, which Callisto passes through.
18	- **Rehearse.** `callisto release --dry-run` shows what would be published and in which order, and works without credentials.
19	
20	## Pulling a release
21	
22	Callisto never deletes, yanks or deprecates anything. Pulling a release is a manual registry action, and the version stays used:
23	
24	| Registry | Soft pull | Delete |
25	| --- | --- | --- |
26	| crates.io | `cargo yank` hides it from new resolution; it stays downloadable and existing lockfiles keep working. | Limited to 72 hours after publishing, or a single owner, few downloads and no dependents. |
27	| npm | `npm deprecate` keeps it installable with a warning. | `npm unpublish` within 72 hours if nothing depends on it; later only with no dependents, under 300 weekly downloads and a single owner. A used version number can never be reused, and removing every version blocks the name for 24 hours. |
28	| PyPI | Yank (PEP 592) hides it from normal resolution. | Permanent. A filename cannot be reused even after deletion, and deleting a project frees its name for anyone. |
29	
30	Registries cache their indexes for minutes, so a pulled version can keep appearing briefly. Prefer the soft pull, then release a fixed, higher version through the normal flow. Leave the git tag in place: Callisto treats an existing tag as a release already made. Yanking does not undo a leaked secret; rotate it.
31	
32	If you remove a version that is still the manifest version, `callisto release` will try to finish it again and stop with an error. Bump the version with a changeset instead.
33	
34	See the registries' own pages for current rules: [cargo yank](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-yank.html), [npm unpublish](https://docs.npmjs.com/policies/unpublish) and the [PyPI help](https://pypi.org/help/).
35	
36	## Where a publish goes
37	
38	A registry with no `url` in `callisto.toml` publishes wherever the checkout's own configuration says: `.npmrc` for npm and `.cargo/config.toml` for Cargo. Callisto honors that on purpose, so a private registry set there keeps working, and it means those files decide where the registry token is sent. Review changes to them like code. A release pull request cannot carry such a change: a version commit may only touch manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets and the decision file, and any other path fails verification with E165. For npm (except yarn) and PyPI, set `url` on the registry entry to pin the destination in `callisto.toml`; Cargo takes its destination only from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a `url` on a cargo registry is rejected.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## npm
43	
44	Two supported patterns.
45	
46	### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`
47	
48	Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:
49	
50	```yaml
51	- name: Authenticate with npm registry
52	  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
53	  env:
54	    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
55	
56	- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
57	```
58	
59	`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.
60	
61	### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`
62	
63	`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:
64	
65	```yaml
66	- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
67	  with:
68	    node-version: '20'
69	    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
70	
71	- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
72	  env:
73	    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
74	```
75	
76	`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.
77	
78	### Choosing a pattern
79	
80	| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
81	| --- | --- | --- |
82	| Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
83	| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
84	| Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
85	| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |
86	
87	### Provenance
88	
89	Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.
90	
91	---
92	
93	## Cargo (crates.io)
94	
95	Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:
96	
97	```yaml
98	env:
99	  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
100	```
101	
102	Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. Inject it only into the job that publishes.
103	
104	---
105	
106	## Python (PyPI)
107	
108	Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):
109	
110	```yaml
111	env:
112	  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
113	  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
114	```
115	
116	Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.
117	
118	The release action maps the `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_USERNAME` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` itself. A workflow that runs `twine` directly must set both, because the secret name alone does not configure Twine.
119	
120	### Generated Callisto workflows
121	
122	Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.
123	
124	Native publish hooks, including `prepare` and `prepublishOnly`, run unchanged with their usual publishing environment.
125	
126	### Current Python support limits
127	
128	Callisto supports static PEP 621 or Poetry versions with `python -m build` and Twine. Current limits:
129	
130	- Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
131	- Without a sealed build, files an earlier attempt uploaded are matched by name, not by content: a rebuild is not always byte-identical. A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
132	- A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
133	- A release can only be completed for 14 days after its first file; after that, PyPI [refuses new files](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/) and the release needs a new version.
134	- A package tagged by an earlier version of callisto with only some of its files uploaded is reported as released when rerun at the same commit. Finish it by uploading the missing files with `twine`.
135	- A configured `url` is the simple index Callisto reads and, unless `publish-url` names another endpoint, the one Twine uploads to. Private indexes with read authentication or HTML-only responses need explicit support. Twine credentials do not authenticate `curl`.
136	- Dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`, Poetry groups and the legacy dev-dependency tables are not followed or rewritten when a workspace package is released. Under uv a version pin on a workspace member is ignored, and Poetry normally references siblings by path, so a stale pin there is harmless; a group that pins a registry version of a sibling is not updated.
137	- `release` refuses snapshot versions (E169), so a snapshot is never published. Python snapshots use a PEP 440 local label (`0.0.0.dev0+<tag>.<sha>`), which public PyPI would reject anyway. See [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).
138
