Crate map, data flow, and the invariants every change must preserve.

--- ## Invariants 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST. String-only `package.json` changes replace scanned literal spans in the original text; other changes keep key order and fingerprinted indentation and line endings. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent directory, and its parent when the call created it; a failed sync is returned unless the filesystem cannot sync a directory) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 6. **Versioning.** The four published crates version in lockstep (one fixed group). Only `callisto-cli`, its command-line interface and its JSON reports are a compatibility surface; `callisto-model`, `callisto-manifests` and `callisto-graph` are internal and may change in any release. 7. **User-facing errors are diagnosable.** Every error surfaced to a user derives `miette::Diagnostic` with a stable code and, where the fix isn't obvious from the message, `help` text. A wrapper around another crate's error (for example `GraphError::Config`) is `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and declares no code of its own, so the inner code reaches the user. Full list: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). Design decisions, with the options they rejected and why: [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md). ## Crate map ``` Layer 1 (leaf) callisto-model Layer 2 (I/O) callisto-manifests Layer 3 (engine) callisto-graph Layer 4 (surface) callisto-cli Dev-only callisto-fixtures ``` | Crate | License | Depends on | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`callisto-model`](crates/callisto-model) | MIT | none (external: `michi-graph`) | Domain primitives (`PackageId`, `Version`, `Severity`, `Changeset`, `PreState`), `atomic_write`, `ApplyPermit`, the `CommandRunner`/`DependencyResolver` trait seams; `format`: `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` parser/writer; `vcs`: `GitAccess`, every Git operation as a subprocess through `CommandRunner` | | [`callisto-manifests`](crates/callisto-manifests) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model | `Manifest` trait; format-preserving Cargo/npm/PyPI manifest editors | | [`callisto-graph`](crates/callisto-graph) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests | Dependency graph, cascade engine, version planning, release execution; `conventional`: Conventional Commit parsing and bump inference; `changelog`: Markdown changelog rendering, with `changelog::markdown` the only place Markdown is scanned; `release_preview`: the serializable view of a plan for the release PR | | [`callisto-cli`](crates/callisto-cli) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model, manifests, graph | `clap` CLI surface, `miette` diagnostic rendering | | [`callisto-fixtures`](crates/callisto-fixtures) | FSL-1.1-MIT | model (dev-only) | Multi-ecosystem test corpus and in-memory test doubles | Dependencies only point down the layers (`cli` → `graph` → `manifests` → `model`). Nothing in Layer 1–3 depends on `callisto-cli`. ## Data flow ``` Workspace::load config::load -> config::resolve callisto.toml -> ResolvedConfig ManifestWalkResolver::build discover (ProjectLocator), read manifests (Manifest), assign ids, attach platform packages, apply per-package config GroupTable::resolve bind [[fixed-group]] / [[linked-group]] members plan_version -> VersionPlan (in memory) aggregate changesets + opt-in commit inference -> severity per package run_cascade dependents (runtime, build, optional, peer; never dev), groups, pre mode -> target version per package, with its reasons version --emit-decision derives and validates the decision in memory, before apply version --emit-preview builds the ReleasePreview (packages, merged changes, findings) from the plan, before apply consumes the changesets it describes apply_version_plan (needs ApplyPermit) CST edits -> atomic_write, changelogs consume changesets -> native lock refresh -> git staging version --emit-decision / --emit-preview writes the decision and the preview files after successful apply compose-pr-body --preview [--publish-plan] renders the release PR body from the preview; --publish-plan adds the outcome of plan_workspace_release_offline on the versioned tree for exactly the packages the preview bumps (never observes a registry) release decision -> intent -> envelope -> execute_release -> receipt per operation observe provider -> adopt, or perform and confirm ``` Package ordering, cycle reports and release-operation readiness all run on `michi-graph` (validation reports every problem at once; edge kinds are chosen per validation). Git access goes through `GitAccess` (`callisto_model::vcs`). Reads that cover every package are batched or run side by side, so a command's cost does not grow by a process or a round trip per package ([release](docs/architecture/release.md) lists them; `just bench` measures them). Depth: - [`docs/architecture/identity.md`](docs/architecture/identity.md): package ids, bare-name matching, config rule specificity, workspace loading, platform packages. - [`docs/architecture/versioning.md`](docs/architecture/versioning.md): plan and apply, file-level idempotence and interrupted-command limits, the release preview and the Markdown module. - [`docs/architecture/release.md`](docs/architecture/release.md): release terms, the two routes, run envelope, observation and proof tokens, the transition table, verification tiers. - [`docs/architecture/wire-compat.md`](docs/architecture/wire-compat.md): the version each release document writes and reads, what a reader does with another, and the known gaps. ## Extension seams Four traits decouple the engine from platform I/O (`callisto-model::exec`, `callisto-model::discovery`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph::locate`): - `ProjectLocator` — enumerates workspace project roots. - `CommandRunner` — runs a subprocess. `run_with_timeout`'s default implementation ignores the timeout; the CLI's runner enforces it, so a hung publish command cannot block forever. - `Manifest` — per-ecosystem read/write. Mutations only touch the in-memory CST; nothing reaches disk until `persist(&ApplyPermit)`, so one open manifest can take several mutations before one write. - `DependencyResolver` — supplies graph nodes and edges; `ManifestWalkResolver` is the only current implementation. ## Current boundaries and planned changes `PackageId` is a flexible selector/display form; `PackageKey` is a directory locator; `ReleasePackageId` is a canonical ecosystem-qualified distribution identity. A directory can own several canonical manifests, but the current package model requires one version grammar. Registry version observations alone do not establish identical package bytes. CI can seal a Python file set in the artifact manifest and verify each file on execution. Remaining v1 work is in [`docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md`](docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md). The canonical-identity and polyglot model is in [`docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md`](docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md); only the parts it marks as design are not implemented, and none is an extension seam. The existing dependency graph and release-operation DAG remain the basis of the plan. ## Not covered here - Release lifecycle, CI plan/build/execute, recovery: [`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md). - Registry authentication: [`docs/publishing.md`](docs/publishing.md). - `callisto.toml` keys: [`docs/config.md`](docs/config.md). - Diagnostic codes: [`docs/errors.md`](docs/errors.md). - Behavior, including `callisto matrix`: [`docs/specs/`](docs/specs/INDEX.md).

# Plan and apply

How `callisto version` turns changesets into file edits, and where interrupted-command recovery stops. Behavior: [`docs/specs/versioning.json`](../specs/versioning.json). Write mechanics: [ADR 8](../adr/0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md). The emitted decision: [ADR 2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md).

## Two phases

| Phase | Entry point | Touches disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan | `commands::plan_version` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs`) returns a `VersionPlan` | No |
| Apply | `apply_version_plan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`) | Yes; takes `&ApplyPermit` |

- `VersionPlan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs`) is the whole change: bumps, dependency spec rewrites, platform manifest writes, owner `optionalDependencies` pins, changelog sections, consumed changesets, `pre.json` updates and diagnostics. It is in memory only (no `Serialize`).
- A changelog section is `## {version}`, a date and compare-link line, then Major, Minor and Patch Changes groups (`[changelog] layout = "grouped"`, the default), or the heading and one bullet list (`"flat"`). `render_section` is pure: the planner puts the layout, the UTC date and the link in `ChangelogInput::style`, and the link needs a GitHub repository (`[release] forge-repository`, else the `origin` remote) plus a tag on the previous version. Readers (`find_section`, `has_heading`, release notes) key on the `## {version}` line only, so they read both layouts; a fixed group's release notes file each member's entries under the bump group the member recorded them in.
- `plan_version` is shared: `version`, `status`, `compose-pr-body` and `release plan --package` all compute the same plan.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/markdown/` is the only place Markdown is scanned: fenced code, ATX headings, heading rebase, the headline split and `Breaking:`/`Action:` markers (`markers.rs`). A new pass asks those questions there and joins `corpus.rs`; it does not write its own line scanner.
- `ReleasePreview` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/release_preview.rs`) is the serializable, versioned view of a plan for people: packages, merged changes, bystanders and findings. Surfaces such as the PR body render it; they do not recompute from the plan. `version --emit-preview` writes it before apply consumes the changesets, and `compose-pr-body --preview` renders from that file. Each changeset change records `pr`, the pull request that added it, read from the first-parent merge commits in one `git log` when the history names one. `ReleasePreview` also carries findings from the changesets (a `Breaking:` or `Action:` marker, a breaking marker whose bump is too low, and no \"backward compatible\" claim when there is a breaking one) and `unreleased`, the publishable packages with source changes since their last tag that the plan does not bump (a package with no tag has no baseline and is not listed) (`version --emit-preview` computes it; a failure to look is a warning). `pr_labels()` derives the managed label catalog, with an `applied` flag per label, from the same findings. `--publish-plan` adds `publish`, the outcome of `plan_workspace_release_offline` on the versioned tree for exactly the packages the preview bumps (the committed decision holds those, not every unreleased package). It never observes a registry or the forge, so the checks that need one (a published version left behind, a name another project owns) are left to the release itself; a refusal becomes a `Stop` finding. `publish.versionedOnly` (optional, absent when empty) names the bumped packages with no publish target, such as a private fixed-group member, which are versioned but never published; the PR body lists them after the publish table. Rows are keyed by the qualified release identity, so `cargo/x` and `npm/x` stay apart.
- `changed_source_files_since_last_tag` lists, per package, the files that differ from its last tag after dropping `DEFAULT_IGNORED_PATHS` (tests, benches, examples, snapshots, Markdown), and `uncovered_changes` returns the changed packages that no pending changeset, nor any member of their fixed or linked group, covers. Neither is wired into the CLI or the PR body yet.
- A dry run never gets a permit, so it reports the plan and never calls apply.
- `snapshot` applies with `ApplyOptions::transient`: manifests are written, while changelogs, changeset deletion and git staging are skipped.

## Idempotent apply

A crash can stop apply after some files are written. Applying the same in-memory plan again is file-level idempotent; a fresh command does not retain that plan.

- Each `PlannedBump` carries `from` and `to`. Before writing a manifest (or a platform manifest), apply reads its current version: `from` means write, `to` means already done, anything else is `UnexpectedManifestVersion`.
- A manifest already at `to` is still staged: the crashed run may have written it without `git add`.
- Apply refreshes affected lockfiles and stages generated version state before consuming changesets or exiting `pre.json`. It stages input deletions with `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before removing the files from disk, so a failed index update leaves the inputs available for recovery. A fresh command does not retain the in-memory plan and can refuse already-stable staged outputs; E121 directs the user to inspect both diffs and finish consuming retained inputs only when the staged outputs are verified. Automatic replay is not guaranteed.
- A Cargo member that inherits its version (`version.workspace = true`) is pinned to a literal version when it is bumped, and `[workspace.package]` is never written, so a member that still inherits keeps the shared version. A bump of every member of a fixed group pins each of them.
- `ApplyOutcome::staged` lists every path apply staged.

## Command boundary and known gaps

`version --emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, applies the plan, and writes the decision only after apply succeeds. The decision file is not wrapped in the stdout report envelope. `--emit-preview` follows the same rules: it is refused with `--dry-run`, built only from a plan without errors, and written after apply succeeds. A relative path for `--emit-decision` is relative to the workspace root, because it names a committed repository file; every other file flag (`--emit-preview`, `compose-pr-body --preview`, and the hidden `release` and `release-pr` flags `--intent`, `--receipt`, `--out`, `--artifact-dir`, `--input`, `--artifact-manifest`, `--source-root`) is relative to `--cwd`, like `git -C`. An absolute path is used as given.

Outside `mode: pre`, `check_partial_run` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's effective version differs from `HEAD` while a changeset remains in `HEAD` or in the working tree (including untracked files), or when a canonical manifest with an effective staged version change is present in the index. Staged metadata-only edits are allowed. During `mode: exit`, prerelease versions awaiting stable finalization remain eligible, but changed stable versions are not exempt from the retry guard. It does not restore a lost plan. Apply retains changesets and pre-state deletion inputs until lock refresh and staging of generated state succeed, then stages their removal before unlinking them from disk. A late `--emit-decision` write failure is actionable refusal, not automatic replay of an in-memory plan that no longer exists.

Apply refreshes each existing lockfile for every ecosystem represented by an actual version, dependency, platform or optional-dependency write, including dual-manifest packages and workspace-root Cargo writes. Cargo lockfiles are refreshed and staged per Cargo workspace, in that workspace's directory. Dependency cascade, co-release floor and snapshot rewrites resolve names in each declaration's native manifest context; pnpm workspace protocols and aliases remain distinct inputs. These behaviors are covered by the [versioning contract](../specs/versioning.json).

# Release wire compatibility

Which version each release document writes, which versions it reads, and what a reader does with any other. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Release types: [`release.md`](release.md). This is a record of current behavior, not a policy; gaps are listed as gaps.

## Documents

| Document | Where it lives | Writes | Reads | Another version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ReleaseDecisionV1` | `.callisto/release-decision.json`; embedded in every intent | 2 | 1 and 2 | Version 1 is accepted and rebuilt in memory as version 2. Any other version fails to decode; reading the committed file reports E166. |
| `ReleaseInputSnapshotV1` | inside an intent only | 1 | any version when decoded alone | Checked only by the intent decoder, which accepts 1 only. |
| `ReleaseIntentV1` | `release plan --out`; the input of `release execute` and `release artifact-manifest` | 5 | 5 | Rejected before any output file is written or provider is touched: E215 from the CLI pre-check, E295 from the model decoder. |
| `ArtifactManifestV1` | `release artifact-manifest --out` | 1 | any version | No decode-time gate. A parse failure is E237; `validate_for_intent` accepts version 1 only. |
| `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` | inside a receipt only | 3 | 3 | Rejected at decode with an `UnsupportedSchema` error that has no diagnostic code. |
| `ReleaseReceiptV1` | `release --receipt`, `release execute --receipt`; also the JSON stdout of both | 2 | 2 | Rejected at decode with an `UnsupportedSchema` error that has no diagnostic code. |

- The decision digest covers the sorted entries (package, target version, reasons) and not the schema version, so a version 1 and a version 2 decision with the same entries share a digest. The digest is verified on every read.
- A receipt is written only when every operation ended `published` or `alreadySatisfied`; a failed run leaves none.
- The release-PR documents (`ReleasePrSnapshotV2`, `ReleasePrDecisionV2`, `ReleasePrConfigV1`, `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1`) are separate types read and written by `release-pr decide`, `release-pr verify` and `release-pr commit-plan`, not by the release decision above. Each accepts exactly its own version. The config, snapshot and decision fail with E155; the commit plan fails with a plain message that has no code.

## Rerun with an older intent

A rerun never reuses an intent from another build. `release execute --intent` and `release artifact-manifest --intent` read the file first and fail with E215 when its version is not 5, before the run envelope is minted. The help says to run `release plan` again. A state file left by an older build is ignored, not read or migrated.

## Readers outside the model crate

- Shell and `jq` readers carry no version gate and depend on shape: the release workflow reads `.artifactSlots` from the intent, the generated build-matrix workflow reads `.operations[].id.package` and `.artifactSlots[]`, and `run-release.sh` reads the receipt's outcome paths.
- `release-pr` snapshots are built by `create-or-update-release-pr.sh` with a hard-coded `schemaVersion: 2`, while the action's `version` input can pin another binary.
- The standalone JSON stdout of `release` and `release execute` flattens the receipt and carries its schema version; the nothing-to-release report is a separate shape with version 1.

## Known gaps

- The snapshot and the artifact manifest have no decode-time version gate of their own.
- The intent decoder's check of the nested decision version cannot fail for a decoded decision, because the decision's decoder normalizes its version to 2 first.
- Two readers tightened without a version bump: the artifact attestation's `sourceCommit` now equals the slot's workflow commit rather than the release source, and decision, operation and slot versions parse with the owning package's ecosystem grammar.
- The receipt's version does not track its nested types: the envelope went from 1 to 3 and the operation role vocabulary grew while the receipt stayed at 2.
- No production code decodes a receipt or an envelope from bytes. Their decode gates and the receipt schema are exercised by tests only.
- A version 1 decision can carry an `unreleasedVersion` reason, which only version 2 defines, and nothing rejects it.
- `callisto schema --type release-receipt` is the only published release schema, and its `schemaVersion` is an unconstrained integer. `callisto schema --type snapshot` is the status report, not `ReleaseInputSnapshotV1`.
- The version 2 intent never existed as its own commit, and the digest transcript version is one constant shared by the decision, snapshot, intent and registry-binding digests.
- The generated consumer workflow passes the intent and manifest between jobs without a checksum or comparison step, which this repository's own release workflow has.

# Release wire compatibility

Which version each release document writes, which versions it reads, and what a reader does with any other. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Release types: [`release.md`](release.md). This is a record of current behavior, not a policy; gaps are listed as gaps.

## Documents

| Document | Where it lives | Writes | Reads | Another version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ReleaseDecisionV1` | `.callisto/release-decision.json`; embedded in every intent | 2 | 1 and 2 | Version 1 is accepted and rebuilt in memory as version 2. Any other version fails to decode; reading the committed file reports E166. |
| `ReleaseInputSnapshotV1` | inside an intent only | 1 | any version when decoded alone | Checked only by the intent decoder, which accepts 1 only. |
| `ReleaseIntentV1` | `release plan --out`; the input of `release execute` and `release artifact-manifest` | 5 | 5 | Rejected before any output file is written or provider is touched: E215 from the CLI pre-check, E295 from the model decoder. |
| `ArtifactManifestV1` | `release artifact-manifest --out` | 1 | any version | No decode-time gate. A parse failure is E237; `validate_for_intent` accepts version 1 only. |
| `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` | inside a receipt only | 3 | 3 | Rejected at decode with an `UnsupportedSchema` error that has no diagnostic code. |
| `ReleaseReceiptV1` | `release --receipt`, `release execute --receipt`; also the JSON stdout of both | 2 | 2 | Rejected at decode with an `UnsupportedSchema` error that has no diagnostic code. |

- The decision digest covers the sorted entries (package, target version, reasons) and not the schema version, so a version 1 and a version 2 decision with the same entries share a digest. The digest is verified on every read.
- A receipt is written only when every operation ended `published` or `alreadySatisfied`; a failed run leaves none.
- The release-PR documents (`ReleasePrSnapshotV2`, `ReleasePrDecisionV2`, `ReleasePrConfigV1`, `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1`) are separate types read and written by `release-pr decide`, `release-pr verify` and `release-pr commit-plan`, not by the release decision above. Each accepts exactly its own version. The config, snapshot and decision fail with E155; the commit plan fails with a plain message that has no code.

## Rerun with an older intent

A rerun never reuses an intent from another build. `release execute --intent` and `release artifact-manifest --intent` read the file first and fail with E215 when its version is not 5, before the run envelope is minted. The help says to run `release plan` again. A state file left by an older build is ignored, not read or migrated.

## Readers outside the model crate

- Shell and `jq` readers carry no version gate and depend on shape: the release workflow reads `.artifactSlots` from the intent, the generated build-matrix workflow reads `.operations[].id.package` and `.artifactSlots[]`, and `run-release.sh` reads the receipt's outcome paths.

# Package identity

How the workspace names packages, why bare names match across ecosystems, and where platform packages are wired in. Behavior: [`docs/specs/workspace.json`](../specs/workspace.json). Config keys: [`docs/config.md`](../config.md). Platform ownership decision: [ADR 7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Dual-manifest package: one directory with several admitted canonical manifests; one graph package, one version grammar and several distribution identities. Cargo+npm is supported by the model; co-located Cargo+Python currently fails with E007 because their grammars differ, including a Maturin dynamic Python version.
- Co-located platform manifest: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in the same directory as its owner's `Cargo.toml`.
- Attached platform package: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in its own directory, owned via another package's `optionalDependencies`.

## `PackageId` (`crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs`)

| Form | Example | `ecosystem()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bare(name)` | `foo`, `@scope/foo` | `None` |
| `Prefixed { ecosystem, name }` | `cargo/foo`, `npm/@scope/foo` | `Some(e)` |

- `parse` treats text before the first `/` as a prefix only when `Ecosystem::from_prefix` knows it, so `@scope/foo` stays bare. It still reads `cargo:foo`; every user-facing input rejects that form with E316 first.
- `display_name` renders a prefixed id as `ecosystem/name`.
- `PackageId` is the display and selector form; `Package::key()` is the workspace-relative directory of the first canonical manifest. It survives display promotion, not a directory move. `ReleasePackageId` names each canonical distribution as `ecosystem/name` using that manifest's own native name.
- Default tags use `display_name()`: `foo@{version}` while bare, `cargo/foo@{version}` after promotion. Promotion therefore also changes the namespace of newly created default tags (ADR 11).
- `matches` is a weak "could be the same package" relation, not equality:
  - Different names never match.
  - A bare id matches any id with the same name, in either direction: bare is an ecosystem wildcard.
  - Two prefixed ids match only when their ecosystems are equal.
- A dual-manifest package can have different native names. `IdentityIndex` resolves each ecosystem/name to its owner; the weak `matches` relation alone does not establish distribution identity or ownership.

## Resolving ambiguity

A workspace can hold `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` as separate packages; ambiguity is resolved where a lookup happens. Qualified selectors work before and after promotion, and the colon form is rejected with E316. Config and CLI selectors must be canonical (`ecosystem/name`); a bare name is E317 (see [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md)).

- `aggregate::resolve_target_package` resolves changeset entries through `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`, which maps qualified native distribution names to their owner and rejects ambiguous bare names. `status` attributes changeset entries and checks their well-formedness through the same resolver.- `[[package]]` rules use `config::resolve::resolve_package_config`: the first rule in declaration order whose ecosystem the package has and whose name matches. It never sorts the rules. Config rejects a rule without its ecosystem (E317), so every rule is ecosystem-qualified.
- `[[package-set]]` is a fallback applied in `ManifestWalkResolver::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`) only when no `[[package]]` rule matched. Patterns (`config/pattern.rs`) are globs over the name with a required ecosystem prefix (a bare pattern is E317), tested against every ecosystem the package has a manifest in.

## Loading a workspace

`Workspace::load` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`):

1. `config::load` reads `callisto.toml` (absent means empty) and calls `config::resolve`, which does all validation and defaulting. Callers holding a `RawConfig` in memory call `resolve` directly.
2. `ManifestWalkResolver::build` discovers projects, assigns ids (`IdentityIndex`), attaches platform packages and applies per-package config.
3. `GroupTable::resolve` binds group members to ids.
4. The tag index is built lazily, on the first `Workspace::tags` call.

A Cargo package inherits from the Cargo workspace that governs it, found the way Cargo finds it (`cargo::enclosing_workspace_manifest`): `package.workspace`, else the nearest manifest at or above the package with a `workspace` table, never above the workspace root. That workspace can be below the root, so the walk, the version guard, release-commit verification, lockfile refresh and `registry_argv` all resolve it per package. Cargo does not judge membership for inheritance, and neither does this lookup: a root that excludes or omits the package is a repository Cargo itself rejects.

`Workspace::load` returns only a complete workspace, and it is the only way to get one. Every manifest the walk cannot open (for its platform role, publish targets or dependencies) is recorded as an error-level `ManifestUnresolved` diagnostic, and `load` turns any of them into E313 naming each manifest once, so no command sees a roster smaller than the repository.

## Historical ownership

For a promoted package, `TagIndex::build` also considers bare-name tags. `history::sole_owner_at` picks the same-named candidate whose first canonical manifest path held a manifest declaring the name at the tag's commit. When none does, because the directory moved or the package gained a higher-priority manifest, it asks which ecosystems had a manifest declaring the shared name at that commit, found with `git grep` and confirmed by reading only the matching manifests. The owner is the one candidate whose own manifest in such an ecosystem has that native name today, taken from the identity index. Two or more matches, or none, mean no owner. `assign_promoted_pre_keys` applies the same check at the commit that added `pre.json`, and E245 reports a baseline with no unique owner. A bare key that matches one current package is checked too: if `pre.json` was added when a manifest of another ecosystem held the name and the package had none, the key pins nothing.

A package that is not promoted checks its own tags the same way: `TagIndex::build` takes the newest `{name}@` tag only if `history::may_have_held_name_at` finds that the tag's commit did not hold a manifest of another ecosystem under the name. A commit with no manifest under the name, or one that cannot be read, is no evidence, so the tag is taken. A rejected tag is reported as `tag-owned-by-another-package` and is not counted as a release of the package.

A demoted package, whose same-named sibling was removed, also considers the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest version across both families.

A rename that changes the native name, or a move that changes it too, leaves no evidence in Git. Declare it with `previous-tag-templates`; do not infer it from the directory key.

## Platform packages in code

| Step | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Find candidates outside the npm workspace globs | `ProjectLocator::projects_and_platform_candidates` |
| Attach a platform to its single owner, or warn | `platform_owners` in `walk.rs` |
| Look up a platform's owner by the platform's own npm name | `IdentityIndex::platform` |
| List an owner's attached platforms (co-located ones excluded) | `IdentityIndex::attached_platforms` |
| Write the owner's version into platform manifests and pin `optionalDependencies` | `platform_version_writes` in `commands/version.rs` (version and snapshot) |
| Publish each platform before its owner | `commands/release/derive.rs`: one `PlatformPublish` operation per attached platform |

- A `PlatformPublish` operation carries the owner's package id and version, so it passes the intent's check that every operation belongs to a decision entry, and each one is a prerequisite of the owner's npm `RegistryPublish`.
- It gets no tag, forge or artifact operation of its own; it publishes by directory.
- Release identities come from `release_package_ids` (`commands/release_decision.rs`): one per canonical manifest, using that manifest's own name, so a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names releases under both.

# Plan and apply

How `callisto version` turns changesets into file edits, and where interrupted-command recovery stops. Behavior: [`docs/specs/versioning.json`](../specs/versioning.json). Write mechanics: [ADR 8](../adr/0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md). The emitted decision: [ADR 2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md).

## Two phases

| Phase | Entry point | Touches disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan | `commands::plan_version` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs`) returns a `VersionPlan` | No |
| Apply | `apply_version_plan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs`) | Yes; takes `&ApplyPermit` |

- `VersionPlan` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/plan.rs`) is the whole change: bumps, dependency spec rewrites, platform manifest writes, owner `optionalDependencies` pins, changelog sections, consumed changesets, `pre.json` updates and diagnostics. It is in memory only (no `Serialize`).
- A changelog section is `## {version}`, a date and compare-link line, then Major, Minor and Patch Changes groups (`[changelog] layout = "grouped"`, the default), or the heading and one bullet list (`"flat"`). `render_section` is pure: the planner puts the layout, the UTC date and the link in `ChangelogInput::style`, and the link needs a GitHub repository (`[release] forge-repository`, else the `origin` remote) plus a tag on the previous version. Readers (`find_section`, `has_heading`, release notes) key on the `## {version}` line only, so they read both layouts; a fixed group's release notes file each member's entries under the bump group the member recorded them in.
- `plan_version` is shared: `version`, `status`, `compose-pr-body` and `release plan --package` all compute the same plan.
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/changelog/markdown/` is the only place Markdown is scanned: fenced code, ATX headings, heading rebase, the headline split and `Breaking:`/`Action:` markers (`markers.rs`). A new pass asks those questions there and joins `corpus.rs`; it does not write its own line scanner.
- `ReleasePreview` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/release_preview.rs`) is the serializable, versioned view of a plan for people: packages, merged changes, bystanders and findings. Surfaces such as the PR body render it; they do not recompute from the plan. `version --emit-preview` writes it before apply consumes the changesets, and `compose-pr-body --preview` renders from that file. Each changeset change records `pr`, the pull request that added it, read from the first-parent merge commits in one `git log` when the history names one. `ReleasePreview` also carries findings from the changesets (a `Breaking:` or `Action:` marker, a breaking marker whose bump is too low, and no \"backward compatible\" claim when there is a breaking one) and `unreleased`, the publishable packages with source changes since their last tag that the plan does not bump (a package with no tag has no baseline and is not listed) (`version --emit-preview` computes it; a failure to look is a warning). `pr_labels()` derives the managed label catalog, with an `applied` flag per label, from the same findings. `--publish-plan` adds `publish`, the outcome of `plan_workspace_release_offline` on the versioned tree for exactly the packages the preview bumps (the committed decision holds those, not every unreleased package). It never observes a registry or the forge, so the checks that need one (a published version left behind, a name another project owns) are left to the release itself; a refusal becomes a `Stop` finding. `publish.versionedOnly` (optional, absent when empty) names the bumped packages with no publish target, such as a private fixed-group member, which are versioned but never published; the PR body lists them after the publish table. Rows are keyed by the qualified release identity, so `cargo/x` and `npm/x` stay apart.
- `changed_source_files_since_last_tag` lists, per package, the files that differ from its last tag after dropping `DEFAULT_IGNORED_PATHS` (tests, benches, examples, snapshots, Markdown), and `uncovered_changes` returns the changed packages that no pending changeset, nor any member of their fixed or linked group, covers. `unreleased_changes` builds `ReleasePreview.unreleased` from them, so the PR body lists the packages they find.
- A dry run never gets a permit, so it reports the plan and never calls apply.
- `snapshot` applies with `ApplyOptions::transient`: manifests are written, while changelogs, changeset deletion and git staging are skipped.

## Idempotent apply

A crash can stop apply after some files are written. Applying the same in-memory plan again is file-level idempotent; a fresh command does not retain that plan.

- Each `PlannedBump` carries `from` and `to`. Before writing a manifest (or a platform manifest), apply reads its current version: `from` means write, `to` means already done, anything else is `UnexpectedManifestVersion`.
- A manifest already at `to` is still staged: the crashed run may have written it without `git add`.
- Apply refreshes affected lockfiles and stages generated version state before consuming changesets or exiting `pre.json`. It stages input deletions with `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch` before removing the files from disk, so a failed index update leaves the inputs available for recovery. A fresh command does not retain the in-memory plan and can refuse already-stable staged outputs; E121 directs the user to inspect both diffs and finish consuming retained inputs only when the staged outputs are verified. Automatic replay is not guaranteed.
- A Cargo member that inherits its version (`version.workspace = true`) is pinned to a literal version when it is bumped, and `[workspace.package]` is never written, so a member that still inherits keeps the shared version. A bump of every member of a fixed group pins each of them.
- `ApplyOutcome::staged` lists every path apply staged.

## Command boundary and known gaps

`version --emit-decision` derives and validates the decision before writes, applies the plan, and writes the decision only after apply succeeds. The decision file is not wrapped in the stdout report envelope. `--emit-preview` follows the same rules: it is refused with `--dry-run`, built only from a plan without errors, and written after apply succeeds. A relative path for `--emit-decision` is relative to the workspace root, because it names a committed repository file; every other file flag (`--emit-preview`, `compose-pr-body --preview`, and the hidden `release` and `release-pr` flags `--intent`, `--receipt`, `--out`, `--artifact-dir`, `--input`, `--artifact-manifest`, `--source-root`) is relative to `--cwd`, like `git -C`. An absolute path is used as given.

Outside `mode: pre`, `check_partial_run` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's effective version differs from `HEAD` while a changeset remains in `HEAD` or in the working tree (including untracked files), or when a canonical manifest with an effective staged version change is present in the index. Staged metadata-only edits are allowed. During `mode: exit`, prerelease versions awaiting stable finalization remain eligible, but changed stable versions are not exempt from the retry guard. It does not restore a lost plan. Apply retains changesets and pre-state deletion inputs until lock refresh and staging of generated state succeed, then stages their removal before unlinking them from disk. A late `--emit-decision` write failure is actionable refusal, not automatic replay of an in-memory plan that no longer exists.

Apply refreshes each existing lockfile for every ecosystem represented by an actual version, dependency, platform or optional-dependency write, including dual-manifest packages and workspace-root Cargo writes. Cargo lockfiles are refreshed and staged per Cargo workspace, in that workspace's directory. Dependency cascade, co-release floor and snapshot rewrites resolve names in each declaration's native manifest context; pnpm workspace protocols and aliases remain distinct inputs. These behaviors are covered by the [versioning contract](../specs/versioning.json).

# How Callisto works

Callisto turns changesets and native package metadata into a version plan. It then coordinates the selected registry, Git, and GitHub operations. Current scope is Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI.

## Where it fits

Use Callisto when contributors should declare release impact and a repo needs native dependency updates across its supported package types. The version plan makes each bump reviewable before publication.

Other tools may fit your existing workflow:

- [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) focuses on npm package releases.
- [Knope](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/) offers configurable release workflows.
- [Nx Release](https://nx.dev/docs/features/manage-releases) integrates with Nx projects and tasks.
- [Release Please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/design.md) builds release PRs from conventional commits.

## A change through the system

Suppose a Cargo crate `service` depends on `core`. A contributor records a change to `core`:

```sh
callisto add --package cargo/core:minor --summary "Add streaming API"
callisto status
callisto version --dry-run
```

Callisto builds the version plan from the changeset, manifests, and `callisto.toml`:

- The changeset requests a minor bump for `core`.
- The Cargo dependency in `service` tells Callisto whether the new version fits its existing requirement.
  - Under the default `out-of-range` policy, a version outside that requirement can bump `service` and update its dependency declaration.
  - Cascade mode and bump severity are configurable.
- Fixed and linked groups can add packages through explicit policy.
- Unrelated npm and Python packages do not join solely because they share the repo.

After reviewing the plan, `callisto version` updates affected manifests, lockfiles, and changelogs. A Cargo package that inherits its version from `[workspace.package]` (`version.workspace = true`) gets a literal version of its own when it is bumped; the shared value is left as it is. It stages the versioned state for a commit. `callisto release --dry-run` then previews the release operations.

## The model

| Concept | What it means today |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace package | A dependency graph node located from source and manifests. |
| Distribution | A native Cargo, npm, or PyPI identity described by a manifest. One package can expose multiple supported distributions. |
| Native dependency | A manifest relationship that can affect dependent versions and publication order. |
| Version group | An explicit fixed or linked rule in `callisto.toml`. |
| Release operation | One registry, tag, GitHub release, or asset effect with prerequisites. |

These relationships serve different purposes. For example, a Rust library embedded in a Python wheel is a build input. That alone does not create a Cargo registry dependency or make the crate and wheel share a version. See [configuration](config.md) for supported dependency and version-group rules.

## Releasing and recovery

- **Local release:** `callisto release --dry-run` previews the plan. `callisto release` runs it from a clean checkout.
  - Native publishers use their own credentials.
- **Managed CI:** The version PR commits the selected package and version decision. CI verifies it after merge.
  - Planning declares operations. Building creates artifacts. Execution receives registry credentials.
- **Execution:** Callisto checks each provider before acting.
  - It adopts an exact match, performs and confirms an absent effect, and stops on a conflict or indeterminate result.
  - A receipt records the evidence collected.

Release operations follow known dependency and platform prerequisites. They do not follow a fixed Cargo, npm, then PyPI sequence. The [release guide](releasing.md) covers the local and CI paths, retries, and recovery.

## Current support

Callisto is pre-v1. These rows describe current behavior rather than planned adapters.

| Ecosystem | Versioning | Publishing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cargo | Crate versions, supported dependency declarations, lockfiles | Cargo |
| npm/pnpm | Package versions, supported native dependency forms, lockfiles | Native npm tooling |
| Python/PyPI | Static PEP 621 or Poetry versions | Build backend and Twine |

| Layout | Current boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Cargo product binaries | Generated CI builds discovered Cargo binary targets. Other products need a user authored builder. |
| napi platform packages | Generated CI supports configured targets and builds only the packages in the release. |
| Co-located Cargo and Maturin | Discovery fails; no generated Maturin workflow. |
| Custom product assets | Declared artifact slots can use a manual CI builder and Callisto's execute route. |

Known release limits matter when choosing a workflow:

- A multi-registry release is not atomic.
- Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Go and NuGet publishers are not available.

Package owners control native lifecycle hooks. Callisto invokes supported tools without rewriting those hooks. See [publishing](publishing.md) for credentials and Python index limits, and [releasing](releasing.md) for the complete operation and recovery rules.

lines: - **Check the name first.** A name another project already owns is rejected by the registry. If it already holds the version you are releasing under another repository, `callisto release` stops with E322 and names that repository. Search the registry before the first release.

- **Fill in the metadata the registry requires.** crates.io needs `description` and `license` (or `license-file`) in `Cargo.toml`. A first release of a crate without them stops with E323 before anything is published.

- **Use a token that can create the package.** A token scoped to existing packages cannot publish a new one. Trusted publishing (OIDC) is configured per package on the registry and generally needs the package, or a pending publisher, to exist first, so plan on one token-based first publish. Follow each registry's current documentation.

-- **Package managers.** An npm package is published with the manager its workspace uses (`npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` 4 or `bun`), passing `--tag`, `--access` and, where the manager takes one, `--registry`. Yarn takes no `--registry`; it reads `publishConfig.registry` from the package itself.

+- **Package managers.** An npm package is published with the manager its workspace uses (`npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` 4 or `bun`), passing `--tag`, `--access` and, where the manager takes one, `--registry`. Yarn takes no `--registry`, and a registry `url` with yarn fails with E168; set `npmPublishRegistry` in `.yarnrc.yml` or `publishConfig.registry` in the package.
- **Scoped npm packages** publish with `--access public` by default. A private scoped package sets `publishConfig.access` to `"restricted"` in its `package.json`, which Callisto passes through.
- **Rehearse.** `callisto release --dry-run` shows what would be published and in which order, and works without credentials.

## What you get

- **Ecosystems:** Cargo, npm, and Python/PyPI. npm packages publish with npm, pnpm, yarn or bun, whichever the workspace uses; Python packages need a static PEP 621 or Poetry version and are built with `python -m build` and uploaded with Twine ([support](docs/how-callisto-works.md#current-support), [credentials](docs/publishing.md)).
- **Native-extension packages:** napi-rs platform packages take their owner's version, the generated workflow builds each `napi.targets` addon, and platform packages publish before the owner. Maturin gets no generated workflow, and Cargo plus maturin in one directory fails with E007 ([releasing](docs/releasing.md#platform-package-publish-order)).
- **Tags:** one per package, `{name}@{version}`, or `ecosystem/name@{version}` when another ecosystem has a package of that name; `tag-template` overrides it ([stability](docs/stability.md), [config](docs/config.md)).
- **GitHub releases:** notes come from the package's changelog section, and the product package's release carries your binary assets ([releasing](docs/releasing.md#generated-workflows)).
- **Supply chain:** the generated build workflow attests each Cargo binary asset with GitHub build provenance, and `release execute` checks its SHA-256 and runs `gh attestation verify` before uploading it; the receipt records each asset's size and SHA-256. npm provenance is on when the publishing job sets `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` ([publishing](docs/publishing.md#provenance)).
- **Release PR:** one PR, rebuilt on every push to the default branch, holds the versions, changelogs and a "Merging will publish" plan. Merging it is the approval ([releasing](docs/releasing.md#release-pr-and-approval)).
- **Safe reruns:** a failed release can be rerun; versions, tags and releases that already landed are adopted, not repeated, and a receipt is written only when every operation succeeded ([publication checks](docs/releasing.md#publication-checks)).
- **Scripting:** every command accepts `--dry-run`, `--format json` reports carry a `schemaVersion`, and a bad flag value exits 2 ([stability](docs/stability.md)).

Dependency-aware, changeset-driven versioning and releases for Cargo, npm, and PyPI monorepos.

--- Callisto turns per-package changesets into a version plan for Cargo, npm/pnpm, and Python/PyPI workspaces. It reads native manifests to decide which dependents need updates, then prepares the files and release operations for review. ## A change through Callisto Suppose `service` depends on a Cargo crate `core` at `^0.2`. A contributor records a minor change to `core`: ```sh callisto add --package cargo/core:minor --summary "Add streaming API" callisto version --dry-run ``` With the default cascade policy, the plan is: | Package | Before | Planned change | | --- | --- | --- | | `core` | `0.2.0` | `0.3.0` from the changeset | | `service` | `1.4.2`, requires `core ^0.2` | `1.4.3` from the default patch cascade; requirement updated to `^0.3` | | Unrelated npm or Python package | Its current version | No bump just because it shares the repo | The dependency requirement triggers the `service` bump; sharing a repo does not. Callisto does not infer arbitrary cross-language dependencies. Explicit version groups can couple packages that should move together. - `callisto version` updates affected manifests, lockfiles, and changelogs for review and commit. - The release workflow uses native publishers and coordinates configured tags, GitHub releases, and assets. Package owners retain their hooks and credentials. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; changesets["Changesets
release intent"] --> plan["Version plan
dependency-aware"] manifests[("Native manifests
Cargo · npm/pnpm · Python")] --> plan plan --> updates["Version updates
manifests · changelogs · lockfiles"] updates --> review{{"Review and commit

configured operations"] release --> outputs(["Packages · tags · GitHub releases"]) class changesets source class manifests store class plan,updates,release engine class review router class outputs output ``` Callisto is pre-v1. The [guide](docs/how-callisto-works.md) covers current support, known limits, and when another tool may be a better fit, and [stability](docs/stability.md) says what will and will not change. ## Install **proto** ([moonrepo/proto](https://moonrepo.dev/proto)), from a release binary: ```toml # .prototools [plugins.tools] callisto = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orin-dx/callisto/main/proto/callisto.toml" ``` ```bash proto install callisto ``` **cargo**, built from source (package `callisto-cli`, binary `callisto`): ```bash cargo install callisto-cli ``` **Release binaries**, from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases) (tag `callisto@`): ```bash curl -sL "https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/download/callisto@/callisto-.tar.gz" | tar -xz ``` Available targets: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`. ## Quick start Start in a Git repository with an `origin` push URL and registry credentials. This example publishes from your machine; to publish from CI instead, keep the workflow `init` writes and see [releasing](docs/releasing.md). ```bash # 1. Detect packages, write callisto.toml and .changeset/, preview the first release. # With a GitHub origin it also writes the release workflow, and it prints what to do next. callisto init --yes --no-workflow # 2. Record a pending change against a package callisto add --package cargo/my-crate:minor --summary "Add authentication middleware" # 3. See pending changesets and the version bumps they imply callisto status # 4. Commit the configuration and pending change git add callisto.toml .changeset/ git commit -m "chore: configure releases and record pending changes" # 5. Consume changesets, bump manifests, update changelogs and lockfiles callisto version # 6. Commit the staged release changes; release requires a clean checkout git commit -m "chore(release): version packages" # 7. Preview, then publish callisto release --dry-run callisto release ``` Drop `--no-workflow` to publish from GitHub Actions instead: a push to the default branch opens a release PR, and merging it publishes. A first release of a Cargo crate needs a `description` and a `license`; Callisto stops with a fix before publishing anything if they are missing. Run `callisto --help` for prerelease mode, snapshots, CI checks, JSON output, and shell completions. ## Documentation - [Guide](docs/how-callisto-works.md): release model, example, and supported layouts. - [Releasing](docs/releasing.md): local and CI workflows, limits, and recovery. - [Publishing](docs/publishing.md): registry credentials. - [Configuration](docs/config.md) and [errors](docs/errors.md): references. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [security](SECURITY.md): project information. ## License Mixed: `callisto-model` is MIT; the rest of the workspace is [FSL-1.1-MIT](LICENSE) (becomes MIT two years after each version's release).

(3) Beyond changesets: release-trigger `auto` infers bumps from conventional commits, with the pre-1.0 `pre-major-inference` policy; prerelease mode (`pre enter` / `pre exit`); throwaway `snapshot` versions; changelog layouts (`[changelog]` grouped|flat) with compare links and layered notes. (4) Releasing: what `callisto release` publishes and the order (platform packages before owners, per-distribution ordering); tags and GitHub releases; product binaries declared with `[release]` / `[[release.artifact]]` and target triples; the one release PR with a 'Merging will publish' plan; confirmation that a published version is visible before tagging; safe reruns; the supply-chain facts you already verified. (7) Platform and install: operating systems and architectures the release binaries cover (read the README install section and the release workflow matrix), and any unsupported platform. 1	# Configuration reference
2	
3	Every key `callisto.toml` accepts, from `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/{raw,resolve,groups}.rs`. Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`).
4	
5	This reference describes current keys, not the unimplemented parts of the [polyglot design](architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Every package named in this file must be written `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name`; a bare name is E317 and the colon form is E316. No release-owner, generic build-input or per-file PyPI configuration exists.
6	
7	## Top-level tables
8	
9	| Table | Type | Required | Meaning |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
12	| `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
13	| `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
14	| `[changelog]` | table | no | Layout of the changelog sections `callisto version` writes |
15	| `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
16	| `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
17	| `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package exact-match overrides |
18	| `[[package-set]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package glob-match overrides |
19	| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
20	| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |
21	
22	## `[changesets]`
23	
24	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
25	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
26	| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |
27	
28	Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.
29	
30	## `[cascade]`
31	
32	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
33	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
34	| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
35	| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
36	| `peer-escalation` | bool | `true` | Escalate peer-dependency bumps into the cascade |
37	| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |
38	
39	Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
40	```toml
41	[cascade]
42	mode = "out-of-range"
43	bump-severity = "patch"
44	peer-escalation = true
45	preserve-npm-ranges = true
46	```
47	
48	## `[validation]`
49	
50	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
51	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
52	| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |
53	
54	## `[changelog]`
55	
56	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
57	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
58	| `layout` | string (`"grouped"` \| `"flat"`) | `"grouped"` | `grouped` writes a date line (with a compare link when the repository is known, from `[release] forge-repository` or else the GitHub `origin` remote, and the previous version has a tag), then `### Major Changes`, `### Minor Changes` and `### Patch Changes` groups, omitting empty ones; dependency updates sit under Patch Changes; a package that only released with its group has no groups, just that line. `flat` writes one bullet list under the version heading, as before layouts existed. Sections already in a changelog are never rewritten. |
59	
60	Example: `layout = "flat"`.
61	
62	## `[release]`
63	
64	Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.
65	
66	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
67	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
68	| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
69	| `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
70	| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |
71	
72	### `[[release.artifact]]`
73	
74	| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
75	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
76	| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
77	| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
78	| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |
79	
80	Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
81	```toml
82	[release]
83	product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
84	forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"
85	
86	[[release.artifact]]
87	package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
88	target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
89	asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
90	```
91	
92	## `[registries]`
93	
94	Keyed by registry name. Three registries are built in, keyed `cratesIo` (kind `cargo`), `npm` (kind `npm`) and `pypi` (kind `pypi`). `cratesIo` and `npm` exist with no URL override even without a `[registries]` table; a `[registries.<built-in>]` entry changes their settings and may leave `kind` out.
95	
96	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
97	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
98	| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321 |
99	| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `npm` it is the registry the publish and the confirmation use (not supported with yarn, which fails with E168: set `npmPublishRegistry` in `.yarnrc.yml`). For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set. A `cargo` registry rejects it with E336: cargo takes its destination from `.cargo/config.toml` |
100	| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
101	| `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
102	| `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |
103	
104	For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.
105	
106	Example:
107	```toml
108	[registries.internal-npm]
109	kind = "npm"
110	url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
111	```
112	
113	## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`
114	
115	Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact ecosystem-qualified id: the package's own name in that ecosystem, which for a dual package can differ per ecosystem (first matching rule wins). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is an ecosystem-qualified glob, compared with each package's name in that ecosystem, and can match many packages at once; a rule for several ecosystems is one rule per ecosystem; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.
116	
117	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
118	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
119	| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact `ecosystem/name`. `[[package-set]]`: `ecosystem/glob`. The ecosystem is `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; a name without one is E317. |
120	| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
121	| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
122	| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
123	| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
124	| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
125	| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |
126	
127	Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
128	```toml
129	[[package]]
130	match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
131	publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
132	tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
133	previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
134	```
135	
136	## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`
137	
138	Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.
139	
140	| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
141	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
142	| `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
143	| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | `ecosystem/name` of each package in the group. A platform package is named by its native name |
144	
145	`[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.
146	
147	Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
148	```toml
149	[[fixed-group]]
150	name = "workspace"
151	members = ["cargo/callisto-model", "cargo/callisto-manifests", "cargo/callisto-graph", "cargo/callisto-cli", "cargo/callisto-fixtures"]
152	```
153	
154	## Identity and defaults
155	
156	Unspecified package fields are filled during graph construction: the release trigger defaults to changesets, the changelog to the package directory, and publish targets to those declared by its manifests. Default tags use the display id, so newly created tags become qualified after name promotion; historical bare tags use the ownership fallback described in [identity](architecture/identity.md). Canonical references alone do not repair the open rename/demotion failures.

| `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package exact-match overrides |
| `[[package-set]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package glob-match overrides |
| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |

## `[changesets]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |

Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.

## `[cascade]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
| `peer-escalation` | bool | `true` | Escalate peer-dependency bumps into the cascade |
| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true
```

## `[validation]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |

## `[changelog]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | string (`"grouped"` \| `"flat"`) | `"grouped"` | `grouped` writes a date line (with a compare link when the repository is known, from `[release] forge-repository` or else the GitHub `origin` remote, and the previous version has a tag), then `### Major Changes`, `### Minor Changes` and `### Patch Changes` groups, omitting empty ones; dependency updates sit under Patch Changes; a package that only released with its group has no groups, just that line. `flat` writes one bullet list under the version heading, as before layouts existed. Sections already in a changelog are never rewritten. |

Example: `layout = "flat"`.

## `[release]`

Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
| `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |

### `[[release.artifact]]`

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
```

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name. Three registries are built in, keyed `cratesIo` (kind `cargo`), `npm` (kind `npm`) and `pypi` (kind `pypi`). `cratesIo` and `npm` exist with no URL override even without a `[registries]` table; a `[registries.<built-in>]` entry changes their settings and may leave `kind` out.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321 |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `npm` it is the registry the publish and the confirmation use (not supported with yarn, which fails with E168: set `npmPublishRegistry` in `.yarnrc.yml`). For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set. A `cargo` registry rejects it with E336: cargo takes its destination from `.cargo/config.toml` |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
| `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
| `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |

For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
```

## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`

Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact ecosystem-qualified id: the package's own name in that ecosystem, which for a dual package can differ per ecosystem (first matching rule wins). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is an ecosystem-qualified glob, compared with each package's name in that ecosystem, and can match many packages at once; a rule for several ecosystems is one rule per ecosystem; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact `ecosystem/name`. `[[package-set]]`: `ecosystem/glob`. The ecosystem is `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; a name without one is E317. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`

Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | `ecosystem/name` of each package in the group. A platform package is named by its native name |

`[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = ["cargo/callisto-model", "cargo/callisto-manifests", "cargo/callisto-graph", "cargo/callisto-cli", "cargo/callisto-fixtures"]
```

## Identity and defaults

Unspecified package fields are filled during graph construction: the release trigger defaults to changesets, the changelog to the package directory, and publish targets to those declared by its manifests. Default tags use the display id, so newly created tags become qualified after name promotion; historical bare tags use the ownership fallback described in [identity](architecture/identity.md). Canonical references alone do not repair the open rename/demotion failures.
