1	# Configuration reference
2	
3	Every key `callisto.toml` accepts, from `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/{raw,resolve,groups}.rs`. Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`).
4	
5	This reference describes current keys, not the unimplemented parts of the [polyglot design](architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Every package named in this file must be written `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name`; a bare name is E317 and the colon form is E316. No release-owner, generic build-input or per-file PyPI configuration exists.
6	
7	## Top-level tables
8	
9	| Table | Type | Required | Meaning |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
12	| `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
13	| `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
14	| `[changelog]` | table | no | Layout of the changelog sections `callisto version` writes |
15	| `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
16	| `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
17	| `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package exact-match overrides |
18	| `[[package-set]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package glob-match overrides |
19	| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
20	| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |
21	
22	## `[changesets]`
23	
24	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
25	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
26	| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |
27	
28	Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.
29	
30	## `[cascade]`
31	
32	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
33	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
34	| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
35	| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
36	| `peer-escalation` | bool | `true` | Escalate peer-dependency bumps into the cascade |
37	| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |
38	
39	Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
40	```toml
41	[cascade]
42	mode = "out-of-range"
43	bump-severity = "patch"
44	peer-escalation = true
45	preserve-npm-ranges = true
46	```
47	
48	## `[validation]`
49	
50	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
51	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
52	| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |
53	
54	## `[changelog]`
55	
56	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
57	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
58	| `layout` | string (`"grouped"` \| `"flat"`) | `"grouped"` | `grouped` writes a date line (with a compare link when the repository is known, from `[release] forge-repository` or else the GitHub `origin` remote, and the previous version has a tag), then `### Major Changes`, `### Minor Changes` and `### Patch Changes` groups, omitting empty ones; dependency updates sit under Patch Changes; a package that only released with its group has no groups, just that line. `flat` writes one bullet list under the version heading, as before layouts existed. Sections already in a changelog are never rewritten. |
59	
60	Example: `layout = "flat"`.
61	
62	## `[release]`
63	
64	Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.
65	
66	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
67	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
68	| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
69	| `forge-repository` | string | none | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to |
70	| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Declared binary artifacts (see below) |
71	
72	### `[[release.artifact]]`
73	
74	| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
75	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
76	| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
77	| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
78	| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |
79	
80	Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
81	```toml
82	[release]
83	product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
84	forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"
85	
86	[[release.artifact]]
87	package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
88	target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
89	asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
90	```
91	
92	## `[registries]`
93	
94	Keyed by registry name. Three registries are built in, keyed `cratesIo` (kind `cargo`), `npm` (kind `npm`) and `pypi` (kind `pypi`). `cratesIo` and `npm` exist with no URL override even without a `[registries]` table; a `[registries.<built-in>]` entry changes their settings and may leave `kind` out.
95	
96	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
97	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
98	| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321 |
99	| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `npm` it is the registry the publish and the confirmation use (not supported with yarn, which fails with E168: set `npmPublishRegistry` in `.yarnrc.yml`). For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set. A `cargo` registry rejects it with E336: cargo takes its destination from `.cargo/config.toml` |
100	| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
101	| `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
102	| `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |
103	
104	For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.
105	
106	Example:
107	```toml
108	[registries.internal-npm]
109	kind = "npm"
110	url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
111	```
112	
113	## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`
114	
115	Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact ecosystem-qualified id: the package's own name in that ecosystem, which for a dual package can differ per ecosystem (first matching rule wins). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is an ecosystem-qualified glob, compared with each package's name in that ecosystem, and can match many packages at once; a rule for several ecosystems is one rule per ecosystem; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.
116	
117	| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
118	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
119	| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact `ecosystem/name`. `[[package-set]]`: `ecosystem/glob`. The ecosystem is `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; a name without one is E317. |
120	| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
121	| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
122	| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
123	| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
124	| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
125	| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |
126	
127	Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
128	```toml
129	[[package]]
130	match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
131	publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
132	tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
133	previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
134	```
135	
136	## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`
137	
138	Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.
139	
140	| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
141	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
142	| `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
143	| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | `ecosystem/name` of each package in the group. A platform package is named by its native name |
144	
145	`[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.
146	
147	Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
148	```toml
149	[[fixed-group]]
150	name = "workspace"
151	members = ["cargo/callisto-model", "cargo/callisto-manifests", "cargo/callisto-graph", "cargo/callisto-cli", "cargo/callisto-fixtures"]
152	```
153	
154	## Identity and defaults
155	
156	Unspecified package fields are filled during graph construction: the release trigger defaults to changesets, the changelog to the package directory, and publish targets to those declared by its manifests. Default tags use the display id, so newly created tags become qualified after name promotion; historical bare tags use the ownership fallback described in [identity](architecture/identity.md). Canonical references alone do not repair the open rename/demotion failures.

name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, moon and the .prototools toolchain, and Callisto CLI'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto installs the requested release version; local builds validated Callisto checkout source and ignores version. Release jobs must use local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: >-
      Version tag of Callisto to install. Default 'latest' installs the release this action's
      own invocation is pinned to (github.action_ref resolved against callisto@ tags), falling
      back to the newest published release when that ref is unset or unresolvable.
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  verification:
    description: >-
      Attestation verification of the prebuilt release asset (gh attestation verify, repo
      orin-dx/callisto, signer workflow callisto-release.yml, source ref refs/heads/main). One of: require = a failed
      verification or missing gh aborts the step and the asset is never run; fallback (default) =
      on failure or missing gh, warn, delete the asset and install from crates.io instead (never
      run the unverified asset); skip = do not verify, warn, and use the asset. Releases built
      before the first attested release carry no attestation, hence the fallback default.
    required: false
    default: 'fallback'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install moon and the .prototools toolchain
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      shell: bash

## Goal

Publish to npm, crates.io and PyPI with no long-lived registry secret in the repository. The CI job proves its identity with a short-lived GitHub OIDC token, and each registry accepts it for a package that names that repository and workflow as a trusted publisher.

## What each registry needs

| Registry | Trusted publisher is set up | The job must | Token reaches the tool by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| npm | per package on npmjs.com: owner, repository, workflow file, optional environment | have `id-token: write`; run npm 11.5.1 or later (Node 24 ships it) | npm detects the OIDC environment itself and prefers it over a token. No secret |
| crates.io | per crate in its settings, after a first manual publish | have `id-token: write`; run `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action`, which exchanges the OIDC token for a short-lived crates.io token and revokes it when the job ends | the action's `token` output, passed to `cargo publish` as `CARGO_
| PyPI | per project on pypi.org: owner, repository, workflow file, optional environment | have `id-token: write`; mint an upload token through PyPI's OIDC exchange | PyPI documents the exchange as an implementation detail; the stable interfaces are `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` and `uv publish`. Tw

A mismatch in owner, repository, workflow file or environment fails, and npm reports it as a misleading E404. Self-hosted runners are not supported by npm. crates.io blocks the `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run` triggers.

## Where Callisto stands

- Generated workflows already give `execute` `id-token: write` (for npm provenance), so the permission itself is not new there. Callisto's own release workflow does not: its policy check allows `id-token: write` only on `build-artifact`.
- Callisto passes the environment through to the tool and never strips `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` or `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`, so npm can see them. ADR 4 keeps authentication with the ecosystem tool, which fits: Callisto does not need to mint tokens.
- The generated action writes a temporary npm config with an `NPM_TOKEN` entry. With no token set that line may stop npm falling back to OIDC. Unverified.
- Twine is the PyPI uploader, and it cannot mint a token.

1. Decide the shape: a `callisto.toml` switch, or a generated-workflow option, for "this registry publishes by OIDC", so no secret input is expected for it.
2. npm: omit the token entry from the generated npm config when OIDC is chosen, and check the pnpm, yarn and bun publish paths. Only `npm publish` is documented to use OIDC, so each package manager must be tested.
3. crates.io: generate the auth-action step before `execute` and pass its output as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.

name: 'Callisto Validate Action'
description: 'Validates pending changesets, package discovery, configuration health, and release plan DAG'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Setup Callisto Environment
      uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto

    - name: Validate Configuration, Package Discovery & Changesets
      shell: bash
      env:
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      # `callisto status --check` exits 0 with no error diagnostics, else 1; `shell: bash` fails the step on it.
      run: callisto status --check

    - name: Pre-Flight Release Plan Simulation (DAG Pre-Check)
      shell: bash
      env:
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      run: |
        echo "::group::Simulating Release Plan"
        callisto release --dry-run --format text
        echo "::endgroup::"

    - name: Render PR Release Pre-Flight Summary
      shell: bash
      env:
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      run: |
        echo "### Callisto Release Pre-Flight Verification" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Package Discovery**: All workspace crates and packages are correctly tracked." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Configuration Health**: \`callisto.toml\` schema and rules are valid." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Changeset Integrity**: Pending changesets are valid." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "#### Workspace Package Status" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        callisto status >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

## What you get

### Versioning from changesets

- Contributors record release intent with `callisto add`, by flags or an interactive wizard. The `.changeset/*.md` files stay compatible with `@changesets/cli` ([stability](docs/stability.md)).
- `callisto status` shows each package's planned bump. `status --check` exits 1 on an error-level diagnostic, so it works as a CI gate ([releasing](docs/releasing.md#pr-pre-flight-verification)).
- `callisto version` bumps manifests, rewrites dependency requirements, writes changelogs, refreshes lockfiles (`--no-refresh-lockfiles` skips that) and stages the result for review ([guide](docs/how-callisto-works.md#a-change-through-the-system)).
- A bump reaches dependents by the `[cascade]` policy: `mode` (`out-of-range` or `always`), `bump-severity`, `peer-escalation` and `preserve-npm-ranges` ([config](docs/config.md#cascade)).
- A mistyped package name gets up to three `did you mean` suggestions, and a wrong ecosystem is caught too ([errors](docs/errors.md)).

### Control over what moves together

- `[[fixed-group]]` members bump in lock-step. `[[linked-group]]` members share the highest severity and align to the highest target version ([config](docs/config.md#fixed-group-and-linked-group)).
- `[[package]]` (exact) and `[[package-set]]` (glob) rules override per package: `release-trigger`, `publish-to`, `tag-template`, `previous-tag-templates` for renamed packages, `changelog` and `pre-major-inference` ([config](docs/config.md#package-and-package-set)).
- `[registries]` adds private or alternate cargo, npm and PyPI registries, each with its own `url`, `publish-timeout` and `confirm-timeout` ([config](docs/config.md#registries)).
- An unknown key in `callisto.toml` is an error, so a typo fails instead of being ignored ([config](docs/config.md)).

### Beyond changesets

- `release-trigger = "auto"` infers bumps from conventional commits. `pre-major-inference` softens them for `0.y` packages: `conservative` turns a major into a minor, and `conservative-feat` also turns a minor into a patch ([config](docs/config.md#package-and-package-set)).
- `callisto pre enter <tag>` and `pre exit` run prerelease mode; the tag must be a valid SemVer prerelease ([errors](docs/errors.md)).
- `callisto snapshot --tag <tag>` writes throwaway versions such as `0.0.0-<tag>-<sha>` without touching changelogs or changesets, and `release` refuses to publish them ([publishing](docs/publishing.md#current-python-support-limits)).
- `[changelog] layout` chooses `grouped` (Major, Minor and Patch Changes under a dated heading, with a compare link when the GitHub repository is known) or `flat` ([config](docs/config.md#changelog)).

### Releasing

- `callisto release` publishes each package whose current version has no tag, using the ecosystem's own tool (`cargo`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun` or Twine), then creates the tag and the GitHub release. `--dry-run` prints the plan first ([releasing](docs/releasing.md#local-release-callisto-release)).
- The order follows dependencies: platform packages publish before their npm owner, and a package's tag and release wait for every one of its registry publishes ([architecture](docs/architecture/release.md)).
- A published version must show on the registry before anything is tagged or announced; `confirm-timeout` sets the wait ([releasing](docs/releasing.md#release-identity-and-recovery)).
